Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `hosted-inference-5xx-spike` (severity: P1)
PagerDuty: Pager 'hosted-inference-5xx-spike' triggered, attempted contact: primary on-call Sam (oncall). Escalation policy: secondary=Amina, manager=Sam M (manager).
Sam (oncall): acking. picking this up now.
Incident Bot: ack failed to register (mobile DND). Escalating to secondary: Amina.
Amina: on it — just woke up, heading to laptop. can someone add quick context (what's failing)? :coffee:
Jae: seeing a spike in 500s from the /v1/generate endpoint across multiple hosts in us-west-2. error rate up ~18% over last 5m. grabbing logs.
Jae: logs snapshot:
```
2026-03-15T02:01:12Z host=inf-03-7 500 runtime_error: kv_cache OOM
2026-03-15T02:01:13Z host=inf-07-2 500 runtime_error: invalid_attention_mask
2026-03-15T02:01:18Z host=inf-05-4 200 ok
```
Ben: looks like a runtime/kernel issue after last runtime tweak (auto-quant patch). I saw similar locally when sequence length > 4k. rolling back the patch to canary.
Erin: customer impact: telemetry shows ~12% of hosted inference requests failing for customers on default model (redwood-13b) in us-west-2; latency also spiking. No billing discrepancies yet but degraded UX.
Sam (oncall): can we route traffic to fallback model or increase autoscale? any quick runbook steps?
Jae: quick checks:
- `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep crash` -> some pods in CrashLoopBackOff
- health endpoint returning 500 on a subset
Runbook step I'm doing: drain affected hosts and redirect traffic to fallback-model-v2.
Ben: issuing canary rollback now. patch revert in flight. command:
```bash
deployctl rollback runtime/auto-quant --to=2026-03-14-rc3 && deployctl restart service inference-router --region=us-west-2
```
Ben: started rollback. ETA ~2m for new pods.
PagerDuty: Escalation: primary unacknowledged; secondary Amina acknowledged at 6178901240. Manager Sam M paged at 6178901245 due to policy.
Amina: confirmed. I'm on the call. starting pod restarts and will flip routing. assigning temporary mitigation: route 30% traffic to fallback-model-v2.
Sam M (manager): I'm awake, standing by for impact and customer comms. if this will be >30m escalate to incident bridge.
Incident Bot: `@Sam M (manager)` requested a temporary suppression window. Use `/incidentbot suppress 30m reason:"mitigation in progress"` to suppress repeated pages.
Sam (oncall): running suppress now. `/incidentbot suppress 30m "mitigation in progress"`
Incident Bot: Suppression confirmed for 30m. PagerDuty notifications will be muted for this incident while suppression is active.
Erin: note for on-call — affected customers list: cust-842, cust-517, cust-nyc-data (small subset). initial outreach drafted.
Amina: routing flip done. verified fallback-model-v2 responses look healthy. error rate drop visible in 60s.
Jae: health probe after routing flip:
```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}" http://inference-usw2/predict
200 0.279
```
Ben: rollback pod readiness passing. kernel revert appears to have removed the OOM traces.
Sam (oncall): good. marking mitigation in place. removing PD noise helps.
PagerDuty: Manager notification: Sam M (manager) acknowledged escalation at 6178901260.
Erin: customer comms ready, sending targeted messages to the three impacted accounts now.
Sam M (manager): thanks team. once we stabilize, let's capture timeline + RCA. Amina, Jae, Ben own remediation and postmortem. Sam (oncall) to coordinate follow-up and customer updates.
Amina: will collect logs + heap profiles and start root cause analysis. plan to roll forward a tested kernel fix and add a preflight for long-sequence workloads.
Ben: will post the quick revert PR link in follow-up and the validation steps I ran.
Jae: adding monitoring alert to detect kv_cache OOM patterns earlier.
Sam (oncall): closing loop for now — mitigation confirmed, customers being notified, PD suppressed. please add any remaining action items to the incident board. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: Incident thread closed for active paging. please file a postmortem issue and set severity+followup.
